question.text: If the minimum subscription is not received in an IPO, by when must the application monies be refunded?

answer.text: Not later than four days from closure of the issue
Within 7 days from closure of the issue
Within 15 days from closure of the issue
Within 30 days from closure of the issue

explanation.text: The Logic: Under SEBI ICDR, if the minimum subscription is not received, all application monies received in the public issue must be refunded forthwith and not later than four days from the closure of the issue. This tight window protects investors from prolonged fund blockage. The Trap: 15 days and 30 days are appealing because they echo other refund-related timelines, but the workbook specifically uses the four-day refund-from-closure rule when minimum subscription fails. Note: "Forthwith" is the operative word — four days is the outer limit, not the target. Delays beyond this attract interest at the stipulated rate.
